reason: The cited evidence (E1-E3) shows that shear-induced ultra-nanocrystalline layers and dynamic amorphization occur in CoCrFeMnNi, but only in near-surface tribological contacts, not in bulk material. There is no evidence for the proposed low-temperature annealing step, its effect on bulk microstructure, or the claimed simultaneous improvements in bulk tensile ductility, Young's modulus, and fracture resistance. The key premises about bulk processing and property enhancements are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Severe plastic deformation (SPD) can refine CoCrFeMnNi to an ultra-nanocrystalline matrix.
Dynamic amorphization occurs at grain boundaries in this alloy under certain conditions.
Low-temperature annealing (300–400 °C) can preserve or induce amorphous grain boundaries without excessive grain growth.
An ultra-nanocrystalline matrix with amorphous grain boundaries simultaneously improves strength, ductility, Young's modulus, and fracture resistance.
The cited evidence demonstrates these microstructural features and property improvements in bulk, processed CoCrFeMnNi.
